name: dev.codevisor/linear
title: Linear
description: Find and manage Linear issues, projects and comments, and wake bots on Linear events.

oauth.userinfoQuery: query Identity { viewer { email organization { id } } }

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: Retrieve an issue attachment by ID. Use format=url to get its title and download URL without fetching the file content. Linear upload URLs are signed for five minutes; call again to refresh. External URLs are returned unchanged. Files embedded in comments have no issue attachment ID; use the URLs in list_comments attachments instead. Download and process documents with your own file tools.

tools.name: prepare_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Prepare a direct Linear file upload for an existing issue.
Uploaded files appear in the issue's Resources; they are not native Linear Documents. To embed a file in Markdown without adding it to an issue's Resources, use prepare_file_upload instead. For written findings or proposals, prefer updating the issue description or using save_document with issue to create an editable Linear Document, unless the user requests a file. The upload workflow creates the Resources link; do not also add the upload URL to save_issue's links field. To revise a file, upload a replacement. To remove its Resources link, use delete_attachment with the attachment ID returned by get_issue. These tools do not edit uploaded file contents, permanently delete stored files, or inspect or change per-file permissions. Explain these limits when relevant.

Workflow:
1. Call this tool with issue, filename, contentType, and size.
2. Upload raw bytes with PUT to uploadRequest.url outside MCP.
3. All headers in uploadRequest.headers are part of the signed request, so send them verbatim.
4. After PUT succeeds, call create_attachment_from_upload with assetUrl to link it to the issue.

Do not base64-encode or transform the file. Use curl --data-binary @path or fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: blob }).
Omitting or modifying any signed header, including casing, will return HTTP 403.
The signed URL must be used within 60 seconds or it will expire.

Upload sequencing:
Prepare, PUT, and finalize one file before calling this tool for another file.
Do not batch multiple prepare_attachment_upload calls before starting the PUTs because earlier signed URLs can expire while later files are prepared.

Example:
curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png \
  -H "content-type: image/png" \
  -H "x-goog-content-length-range: N,N" \
  -H "cache-control: public, max-age=31536000" \
  -H 'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="file.png"' \
  "<uploadRequest.url>"

tools.name: prepare_file_upload
tools.description:
Prepare a direct Linear file upload to embed an image or file in a Markdown field.
The file is not added to any issue's Resources. To attach a file to an issue's Resources, use prepare_attachment_upload.

Workflow:
1. Call this tool with filename, contentType, and size.
2. Upload raw bytes with PUT to uploadRequest.url outside MCP.
3. All headers in uploadRequest.headers are part of the signed request, so send them verbatim.
4. After PUT succeeds, put markdown (or assetUrl) in the body of save_diff_comment, update_diff, submit_diff_review, save_comment, save_document, save_project, or another Markdown field.

Do not base64-encode or transform the file. Use curl --data-binary @path or fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: blob }).
Omitting or modifying any signed header, including casing, will return HTTP 403.
The signed URL must be used within 60 seconds or it will expire.

Upload sequencing:
Prepare and PUT one file before calling this tool for another file.
Do not batch multiple prepare_file_upload calls before starting the PUTs because earlier signed URLs can expire while later files are prepared.

Example:
curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png \
  -H "content-type: image/png" \
  -H "x-goog-content-length-range: N,N" \
  -H "cache-control: public, max-age=31536000" \
  -H 'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="file.png"' \
  "<uploadRequest.url>"

tools.name: create_attachment_from_upload
tools.description:
Link an already-uploaded Linear assetUrl to an existing issue as an attachment.
Uploaded files appear in the issue's Resources; they are not native Linear Documents. To embed a file in Markdown without adding it to an issue's Resources, use prepare_file_upload instead. For written findings or proposals, prefer updating the issue description or using save_document with issue to create an editable Linear Document, unless the user requests a file. The upload workflow creates the Resources link; do not also add the upload URL to save_issue's links field. To revise a file, upload a replacement. To remove its Resources link, use delete_attachment with the attachment ID returned by get_issue. These tools do not edit uploaded file contents, permanently delete stored files, or inspect or change per-file permissions. Explain these limits when relevant.

Use this only after:
1. prepare_attachment_upload returned an assetUrl and uploadRequest.
2. The client successfully PUT raw file bytes to uploadRequest.url.

This tool does not upload file content. It only creates the Linear attachment row.
If the direct upload failed or the signed URL expired, rerun prepare_attachment_upload and upload again.

tools.name: create_attachment
tools.description:
Deprecated fallback for tiny files only. Accepts base64 file content, verifies SHA-256 checksum, and uploads it through the MCP worker.
Prefer `prepare_attachment_upload` plus direct PUT plus `create_attachment_from_upload`.
Uploaded files appear in the issue's Resources; they are not native Linear Documents. To embed a file in Markdown without adding it to an issue's Resources, use prepare_file_upload instead. For written findings or proposals, prefer updating the issue description or using save_document with issue to create an editable Linear Document, unless the user requests a file. The upload workflow creates the Resources link; do not also add the upload URL to save_issue's links field. To revise a file, upload a replacement. To remove its Resources link, use delete_attachment with the attachment ID returned by get_issue. These tools do not edit uploaded file contents, permanently delete stored files, or inspect or change per-file permissions. Explain these limits when relevant.

CRITICAL: Do not print base64Content and then copy it into this tool call.
Opaque base64 copied through model-visible text is easy to corrupt.

Generate base64Content mechanically from the source bytes and pass it through a programmatic argument construction path whenever available. Before calling this tool, verify the values are consistent:

Unix-like shells:
file="/path/to/file"
base64Content=$(base64 < "$file" | tr -d '\n\r')
sha256=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
decodedSha256=$(printf '%s' "$base64Content" | base64 -d | shasum -a 256 | awk '{print $1}')
size=$(wc -c < "$file" | tr -d ' ') # optional; stat can also get file byte size
decodedSize=$(printf '%s' "$base64Content" | base64 -d | wc -c | tr -d ' ')

PowerShell:
$file = 'C:\path\to\file'
$bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($file)
$base64Content = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
$sha256 = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $file).Hash.ToLower()
$size = $bytes.Length # optional
$decoded = [Convert]::FromBase64String($base64Content)
$decodedStream = [IO.MemoryStream]::new($decoded)
$decodedSha256 = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -InputStream $decodedStream).Hash.ToLower()
$decodedSize = $decoded.Length

decodedSha256 must equal sha256. If you pass size, decodedSize must equal size.
Pass `sha256`. Passing `size` is optional, but recommended for clearer mismatch errors.

tools.name: delete_attachment
tools.description: Remove an attachment link from an issue's Resources. This does not delete the stored file. Use the attachment ID from get_issue's attachments array, not a UUID from the upload URL.

tools.name: list_agent_skills
tools.description: List Linear Agent skills available to the authenticated user.

tools.name: get_agent_skill
tools.description: Retrieve a Linear Agent skill by ID, including its full markdown instructions.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. `statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

tools.name: save_comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description: Delete a Linear comment. Inline description comments (those with non-null `quotedText`) anchor a mark in the editor, so their root cannot be deleted — delete the replies individually or resolve the thread instead.

tools.name: list_cycles
tools.description: List a team's cycles with their IDs, numbers, dates, and issue and scope histories

tools.name: list_custom_views
tools.description: Find saved issue, project, and initiative views accessible to the user, including personal, workspace, and team views. Excludes archived views and views scoped to a project or initiative. Returns view metadata, not the records matching its filters.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Retrieve a Linear document by ID or slug

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List documents in the user's Linear workspace

tools.name: save_document
tools.description: Create or update a Linear document. If `id` is provided, edits the existing document; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `title` is required and exactly one parent (`project`, `issue`, `initiative`, `cycle`, or `team`) must be specified. On update, passing a parent reparents the document. To change parts of the content without resending all of it, pass `patch` instead of `content`.

tools.name: extract_images
tools.description: Extract and fetch images from markdown content. Use this to view screenshots, diagrams, or other images embedded in Linear issues, comments, or documents. Pass the markdown content (e.g., issue description) and receive the images as viewable data.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage. A nonempty fields selection overrides the include options; request optional fields directly in fields.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List issues in the user's Linear workspace, including active Triage Intelligence suggestions for issues in triage. For issues assigned to me, use "me" as the assignee. For issues created by me, use "me" as the creator. Use "null" for no assignee.

tools.name: save_issue
tools.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

tools.name: list_issue_statuses
tools.description: List available issue statuses in a Linear team

tools.name: get_issue_status
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue status in Linear by name or ID

tools.name: list_issue_labels
tools.description: List available issue labels in a Linear workspace or team. A retired label carries `retiredAt` and cannot be applied to new issues.

tools.name: save_issue_label
tools.description: Create or update a Linear issue label. If `id` is provided, updates the existing label; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` is required.

tools.name: create_issue_label
tools.description: Create a new Linear issue label. Deprecated: use `save_issue_label`, which can also update labels.

tools.name: retire_issue_label
tools.description: Retire a Linear issue label so it cannot be applied to new issues. The label stays visible on issues that already have it. Retiring a label group also retires its child labels. Undo with `restore_issue_label`.

tools.name: restore_issue_label
tools.description: Restore a retired Linear issue label, making it available for use on issues again. Restoring a label group also restores every child label, including any that were retired separately.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List projects in the user's Linear workspace

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Retrieve details of a specific project in Linear

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Create or update a Linear project. If `id` is provided, updates the existing project; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` and at least one team (via `addTeams` or `setTeams`) are required. Pass `template` to create the project from a project template. To change parts of the description without resending all of it, pass `patch` instead of `description`. `state` resolves against the project statuses of the lead team, so pass `leadTeam` when creating a multi-team project whose teams use different statuses.

tools.name: list_project_labels
tools.description: List available project labels in a Linear workspace or team. Returns workspace labels by default; pass `team` to also include that team's labels. Pass `includeGroups` to include groups, which return `groupType`; child labels return their `parent` and `parentGroupType`. A team-scoped label carries a `team` field; different teams can hold same-named labels, so check it before acting on an ID. A retired label carries `retiredAt` and cannot be applied to new projects.

tools.name: retire_project_label
tools.description: Retire a Linear project label so it cannot be applied to new projects. The label stays visible on projects that already have it. Retiring a label group also retires its child labels. Undo with `restore_project_label`.

tools.name: restore_project_label
tools.description: Restore a retired Linear project label, making it available for use on projects again. Restoring a label group also restores every child label, including any that were retired separately.

tools.name: save_project_label
tools.description: Create or update a Linear project label. If `id` is provided, updates the existing label; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` is required.

tools.name: list_release_pipelines
tools.description: List release pipelines in the workspace.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: List releases in the workspace, with optional filtering by pipeline, stage, version, and text.

tools.name: get_release
tools.description: Retrieve details of a release by ID or slug.

tools.name: save_release
tools.description: Create or update a release. If `id` is provided, updates the existing release; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` and `pipeline` are required. Release status is modeled as the release pipeline stage.

tools.name: list_release_notes
tools.description: List release notes in the workspace, optionally filtered by pipeline or covered release.

tools.name: get_release_note
tools.description: Retrieve release notes by ID or slug, including markdown content.

tools.name: save_release_note
tools.description: Create or update release notes. If `id` is provided, updates the existing release notes; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `pipeline` and either `releases` or a release range are required. To change parts of the content without resending all of it, pass `patch` instead of `content`.

tools.name: share_issue
tools.description: Share an issue with a workspace user who cannot otherwise access it. Use this tool only when the user explicitly asks to share the issue.

tools.name: unshare_issue
tools.description: Remove a workspace user's shared access to an issue. Use this tool only when the user explicitly asks to stop sharing the issue.

tools.name: list_milestones
tools.description: List all milestones in a Linear project

tools.name: get_milestone
tools.description: Retrieve details of a specific milestone by ID or name

tools.name: save_milestone
tools.description: Create or update a milestone in a Linear project. If `id` is provided, updates the existing milestone; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` is required.

tools.name: get_notifications
tools.description: Get a page of notifications from the authenticated user's Linear inbox.

tools.name: mark_notification
tools.description: Mark a Linear inbox notification as read or unread, or snooze or unsnooze it.

tools.name: list_teams
tools.description: List teams in the user's Linear workspace, including their parent IDs and hierarchy names

tools.name: get_team
tools.description: Retrieve details of a specific Linear team, including its parent ID and hierarchy name. Use list_teams with parentTeam or ancestorTeam to find its sub-teams

tools.name: get_triage_responsibility
tools.description: Retrieve who is responsible for a team's triage: the person on triage now, what happens when an issue enters triage, and the upcoming shifts of the team's triage rotation. Pass `user` to get only that person's shifts, for example to find when their next triage duty starts, even when it is weeks away.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the Linear issue, project, and document templates available to the authenticated user. Use this to find the template a team expects, then call get_template for its content.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Retrieve a Linear template by ID or name: the content it pre-fills, the ids it applies, its sub-issues, and its form fields. Pass the template to save_issue or save_project to apply it. References come back as ids, so read a name with the matching tool when you need one. A form template collects its answers through a form, so applying one here creates an issue with the form unanswered.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List workspace users with their IDs, names, emails, and admin, guest, and active flags. Use get_user for team memberships.

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Retrieve one user's profile, email, admin, guest, and active flags, plus team IDs, names, and keys. Use list_users to find matching users.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Retrieve the connected workspace's ID, name, and URL to confirm which workspace you are using

tools.name: search_documentation
tools.description: Search Linear's product documentation for feature and usage guidance. Returns up to five results with titles, URLs, and content snippets per page.

tools.name: get_diff
tools.description: Exact lookup for a Linear diff. Use with review URLs, GitHub PR URLs, Linear full identifiers, UUIDs, or slugs.

tools.name: list_diffs
tools.description: List Linear diff pull requests visible to the authenticated user

tools.name: get_diff_threads
tools.description: Exact lookup for diff threads and the authenticated user's drafts. Use with review URLs, GitHub PR URLs, Linear full identifiers, UUIDs, or slugs.

tools.name: save_diff_comment
tools.description: Create, reply to, or edit a comment or persisted draft on a Linear diff. Set draft to true to save without submitting. Provide draftId to edit or submit a persisted draft, and commentId only to edit a submitted comment. Submitting an inline draft reuses its saved anchor; submitting a reply draft requires parentId again.

tools.name: resolve_diff_thread
tools.description: Resolve or reopen a top-level comment thread on a Linear diff

tools.name: delete_diff_comment
tools.description: Delete a comment or persisted draft from a Linear diff

tools.name: submit_diff_review
tools.description: Approve a Linear diff, request changes, or submit a review comment

tools.name: update_diff
tools.description: Update a Linear diff's title, description, reviewer requests, issue links, or status. Provide at least one update. Combined updates can partially succeed; inspect the result before retrying. Use merge_diff to merge and submit_diff_review to approve or request changes.

tools.name: merge_diff
tools.description: Merge a Linear diff or add it to the repository's merge queue

tools.name: list_customers
tools.description: List customers in the user's Linear workspace

tools.name: save_customer
tools.description: Create or update a Linear customer. If `id` is provided, updates the existing customer; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` is required.

tools.name: delete_customer
tools.description: Delete a customer in Linear

tools.name: list_customer_needs
tools.description: List customer needs (customer requests) for an issue, project, or initiative. Provide exactly one of `issue`, `project`, or `initiative`. Project results include requests linked to the project's issues; initiative results include requests on projects in the initiative or any of its sub-initiatives, and on their issues. Returns requests on closed work too; each need includes its issue's workflow state and its project's status so callers can filter. Paginated; pass `cursor` from the previous page to fetch the next.

tools.name: save_customer_need
tools.description: Create or update a customer need (request) in Linear. If `id` is provided, updates the existing need; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `body` is required.

tools.name: delete_customer_need
tools.description: Archive a customer need (request) in Linear

tools.name: list_initiatives
tools.description: List initiatives in the user's Linear workspace

tools.name: get_initiative
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific initiative in Linear

tools.name: save_initiative
tools.description: Create or update a Linear initiative. If `id` is provided, updates the existing initiative; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` is required. To change parts of the description without resending all of it, pass `patch` instead of `description`.

tools.name: list_initiative_labels
tools.description: List available initiative labels in the Linear workspace. Pass `includeGroups` to include groups, which return `groupType`; child labels return their `parent` and `parentGroupType`. A retired label carries `retiredAt` and cannot be applied to new initiatives.

tools.name: save_initiative_label
tools.description: Create or update a Linear initiative label. If `id` is provided, updates the existing label; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `name` is required.

tools.name: create_initiative_label
tools.description: Create a new Linear initiative label. Deprecated: use `save_initiative_label`, which can also update labels.

tools.name: retire_initiative_label
tools.description: Retire a Linear initiative label so it cannot be applied to new initiatives. The label stays visible on initiatives that already have it. Retiring a label group also retires its child labels. Undo with `restore_initiative_label`.

tools.name: restore_initiative_label
tools.description: Restore a retired Linear initiative label, making it available for use on initiatives again. Restoring a label group also restores every child label, including any that were retired separately.

tools.name: get_status_updates
tools.description: List or get project/initiative status updates with their body, health, author, and parent project or initiative. Pass id to get one update and ignore list filters; omit id to list.

tools.name: save_status_update
tools.description: Create or update a project/initiative status update and return the saved update. To create, omit id and provide body plus project or initiative matching type. To update, provide id; project and initiative are ignored.

tools.name: delete_status_update
tools.description: Delete (archive) a project or initiative status update.

events.name: issue.created
events.description: An issue was created in a Linear team you can see. Filter on issue.team.key, issue.project.name, assignedToMe or byMe.

events.name: issue.updated
events.description: An issue changed: its status, assignee, priority, title, labels, project and so on. `changes` lists what changed (for example "status" in changes) and `from` holds the previous status, assignee and priority.

events.name: comment.created
events.description: Someone commented on an issue. mentionsMe is true when the comment mentions you.

events.name: mention.created
events.description: Someone else mentioned you in a comment or in a new issue's description. source is "comment" or "issue"; comment is null for issues.

skills.name: linear
skills.description: Work in the user's Linear workspace: find and update issues, comment, and react to Linear events with filters.
